# pingtable

> pingtable pings many hosts, checks whether TCP ports are listening, and
> traces routes. It is a small free Windows program (Rust, Apache-2.0) with a
> window app, a command-line program, a local HTTP API and an MCP server, so a
> person, a script or an AI agent can all use the same checks.

Checks are sent from the computer pingtable runs on. Use it only on hosts the
user owns or is allowed to test.

## For agents

- [Using pingtable from an AI agent](https://github.com/lorincz-llc/pingtable/blob/main/docs/ai-agents.md): the MCP server (`pingtable-cli mcp`), its six tools with arguments and example results, which tool to use when, limits.
- [The local HTTP API](https://github.com/lorincz-llc/pingtable/blob/main/docs/api.md): every call with request and reply examples; `pingtable-cli api` prints the address and token.

## Quick reference

- MCP server command: `pingtable-cli mcp` (standard input and output; tools only).
- Tools: `ping`, `check_ports`, `trace_route`, `network_info`, `table_status`, `table_add_hosts`.
- Command line with JSON: `pingtable-cli once --format json HOST...`, `pingtable-cli ports --format json HOST [PORT...]`. Exit status 0 when everything answered, 1 when not, 2 for a bad command.
- Port check results: `open` (listening), `closed` (host refused), `no_answer` (firewall, or host off).
- A ping with no answer does not prove a host is off; many hosts drop pings. Check a port it should serve.
